// z 9). Rows run along +x, successive rows along +z. The partition at x 33 (door at z 11), the ladder top at x 34
// z 10, the stair-joiner's fence posts at x 35 z 16..19 and the walls are not written: their cells are left alone.
// Lanes: door (33,11) and ladder top (34,10) to the desk and chair, down the west part, and the east strip stays open.
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

const LEGEND = {
  S: "spruce_fence",
  T: ["spruce_slab", { type: "bottom" }],
  C: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "south", half: "bottom" }],
  K: "bookshelf",
  Z: ["barrel", { facing: "up", open: "false" }],
  H: ["chest", { facing: "west", type: "single", waterlogged: "false" }],
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
  A: "potted_azalea_bush",
};

// y 19: floor-level furniture (x 26..36 across, z 9..23 down)
const FLOOR = [
  "....S.S....",
  ".....C.....",
  "..........K",
  "K.........K",
  "K.........K",
  "K..........",
  "K..........",
  "K..S.......",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "Z..........",
  ".........H.",
  "......H....",
  "...........",
];

// y 20: desk top, table top, shelf tops, lanterns on barrel and chests
const TOP = [
  "....TTT....",
  "...........",
  "..........K",
  "K.........K",
  "K.........K",
  "K..........",
  "K..........",
  "K..T.......",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "L..........",
  ".........L.",
  "......L....",
  "...........",
];

// y 21: the lamps on the desk and the table, and a flower pot on the desk
const LAMPS = [
  "....L.A....",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...L.......",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
];

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, [26, 19, 9], LEGEND, [FLOOR, TOP, LAMPS]);
}

input.summary:
H1 loft furnished as an attic study: a desk under the gable window (lantern and azalea pot on it), a chair, a table lamp in the middle, bookshelves on the west and east walls, barrel, chests and lanterns; 34 blocks in parts/room-4.mjs via layers().
make.sh is whole (13126 cells) with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. `mcd room` with rooms-build.json says OK: 155 of 164 floor cells reachable (the 9 unreached are tops of furniture), light min 7 with 0 dark cells and 2 dim.
room.png (from above and inside) reads as a study with the desk as focal piece; the loft floor itself is the shell's dark brown, not my part.
left: plan.md has no per-part checkbox for the H1 loft and elements.md has no loft-specific item (the gable window is frontage's), so nothing was ticked.

The instructed `mcd room ... --rooms rooms.json` reads the world-frame box against the file's shifted y, so it reports a stale NEEDS WORK with no furniture shown; the correct check is --rooms rooms-build.json.
2 floor cells stay dim (light 1-7) at the east north corner; a lantern at (35,19,11) would lift them, but I kept the current layout since the verdict is OK with min 7.
The loft is a room with no carpet, bed or rug: the palette has no carpet or bed, so the study has no rug and no bed.

waste.what: Worked out the floor layout cell by cell in the x/z grid, converting between the plan grid's columns and world x (origin x 26, z 9) and checking each row by hand for length.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of drafting 15 rows x 3 layers as text, one failed frame guess
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --rooms` variant that prints the floor grid with an x/z ruler in world coordinates and writes a legend-ready template for layers() would have saved the column counting.

waste.what: Chased a frame mismatch: plan and room used rooms.json (world y) while build.nbt is saved shifted by YOFF=5, so the first room check said NEEDS WORK with my furniture invisible and the light map unchanged.
waste.cost: 2 extra make/check cycles and a manual peek script with the y offset
waste.tool: mcd room/plan/rooms should read the frame from build.mjs (rooms-build.json) or accept a --yoff flag, so the instructed command works as written.

waste.what: Peeked single blocks with a throwaway node script to confirm what was placed.
waste.tool: `mcd blocks-at build.nbt x,y,z` (or `mcd room` listing furniture cells with their block ids) would do this in one call.

companions.task: Detail the desk and bookcases: which faces get trapdoor drawers, slab tops and chair-stair backs, so the pieces read as furniture from the lane rather than as blocks on the floor.
Place the lights with the room tool's lantern spots before furnishing, so the two remaining dim corners in the east strip get a lantern without taking a lane cell.
